newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian avg lending rate slides to 9.0 vs 9.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian avg lending rate slides to 9.0 vs 9.2 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate fell a further 20 basis points to 9.0 percent on Monday on moderate interbank demand.
Trade totalled 56.2 million kuna, of which 17.7 million were old short-term loans rolled over by creditors.
The interbank call money was steady at 8.0 percent, which it fell to last week as demand slackened from 10 percent previously.

Term rates ranged between 11 and 12 percent for one-week funds and 13-16 percent for two weeks, depending on borrowers. Savings banks are charged higher prices than commercial banks because of a perceived repayment risk.
Insurers renewed one-week deals at a steady 9.0 percent.

The central bank's kuna midrates for Tuesday eased to 6.2216 versus 6.1665 against the dollar and strengthened to 3.5656 versus 3.5700 against the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
